description: Work out the income tax relief on UK pension contributions in a tax year, for someone self-employed, employed or both, in Scotland or the rest of the UK: the 20% a personal pension or SIPP adds at source, the higher or additional rate relief still to claim and how, or the relief a workplace net pay scheme gives through payroll, and the net cost. Relief stops at the higher of £3,600 and the year's earnings, and the annual allowance is checked. Earlier tax years still open for a claim can be priced, with the deadline and route for claiming missed relief. Amounts are gross (what reaches the pension) unless contributionIs is "paid". Salary sacrifice is not covered.

contributionIs.description: Relief at source only: amounts are gross in the pot (default) or what was paid in

currentPensionContribution.description: Personal pension contributions now, a year

employerContributions.description: Employer contributions, a year (count towards the annual allowance only)

flexiblyAccessed.description: True if taxable money has been taken flexibly from a pension (money purchase allowance)

method.description: relief-at-source (personal pension, SIPP, many workplace schemes; the default) or net-pay (workplace scheme taken from pay before income tax)

otherIncome.description: Other non-savings income, such as rental profit or a pension received

salary.description: Employment income before any pension deduction

scottishTaxpayer.description: True for a Scottish taxpayer (Scottish bands)

targetPensionContribution.description: Personal pension contributions planned, a year (for an earlier year, what was paid in)

taxYear.description: UK tax year, e.g. "2026-27"; earlier years price relief that was never claimed. Defaults to the current one.

taxpayer.description: Defaults from the incomes given: both, employed (salary only) or self-employed

name: calculate_pension_tax_relief
title: Calculate pension tax relief
